title: Singular -us/-ys words retaining s
summary: For this -us/-ys family, keep final s and add -ta/-tä: kysymys (“question”) → kysymystä.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

In this selected kysymys-type family, keep final s and add -ta/-tä. Words with similar final letters can use a different singular pattern, so learn the family with the word. The next lesson teaches the contrasting singular pattern.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Keep kysymys and add -tä: kysymys → kysymystä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “question”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep vastaus and add -ta: vastaus → vastausta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “answer”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep ajatus and add -ta: ajatus → ajatusta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “thought”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep kokous and add -ta: kokous → kokousta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “meeting”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep harjoitus and add -ta: harjoitus → harjoitusta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “exercise”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not apply the contrasting -tta/-ttä pattern here.
Select a/ä from the complete word.
